questions.text: Write a short note on the life of Prophet Muhammad.
questions.text_as_printed: Write a short note on the life of Prophet Muhammad. (A)

answer.value:
Born in 570 CE in Mecca, Muhammad’s parents were Abdullah and Amina.
He was raised under the care of his uncle.
He traveled extensively for his trade.
After some time in Mecca, Muhammad was employed to serve in the household of a wealthy widow.
Later, he married this widow.
They had two sons and four daughters.
Muhammad had a habit of solitary contemplation and meditation.
He meditated in the Hira cave near Mecca.
Once, while meditating, he heard the voice of an angel.
The angel declared Muhammad as Allah’s prophet.
He conveyed the divine truths he received.
His followers compiled these teachings into the Quran, the holy book of Islam.
The traditional community in Mecca began opposing the Prophet.
In 622 CE, he migrated from Mecca to Medina, an event known as the Hijra.
A few years later, he passed away in 632 CE.

He defeated Goliath, who was much stronger, and became the king of the Jews.
His son, the famous King Solomon, ruled for a long time and built the first Jewish temple.
After Solomon’s death, the kingdom split into two: Israel and Judah.
Over the next several centuries, Israel and Judah faced continuous attacks.
As a result, Jews settled not only in the Middle East but also in Europe, Asia, and Africa.
The Jewish civilization is a story of struggle for survival.
During World War II, German dictator Adolf Hitler killed 6 million Jews.
After World War II, with the help of the United Nations, a separate nation, Israel, was established for the Jews.
Thus, Jews scattered worldwide regained their homeland after 3,000 years.
The sacred book of the Jews is the Hebrew Bible, also called the “Old Testament.”

questions.text: Explain the life of Jesus Christ.
questions.text_as_printed: Explain the life of Jesus Christ. (A)

answer.value:
Jesus’ birthplace was Bethlehem, 5 km from Jerusalem in the province of Judea.
Jesus was the only son of a poor couple, Joseph and Mary.
Jesus was proficient in Aramaic and Semitic languages.
At that time, Jews were expecting the arrival of a “Messiah” or “Great Savior.”
This idea was propagated by a person named John, a religious preacher.
John baptized people who came to him.
Jesus Christ was also baptized by John, who declared him the “Messiah” or “Great Savior.”
At that time, Jesus was 30 years old and began preaching and teaching across Israel.
Over time, Jews accepted Jesus as their religious leader.
Jesus initially had 12 disciples, known as the Apostles.
